result.title: Ground, Guide, Act: Improving VLA Spatial Generalization with Multimodal Foundation Models
result.summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models effectively learn action policies from robot demonstrations, but struggle to generalize to changes in object positions and task goals. General multimodal foundation models (MFMs) offer complementary scene understanding and spatial reasoning, but remain slow and unreliable for direct fine-grained control. To understand how MFMs can improve VLA spatial generalization, we conduct a systematic capability analysis across multiple VLA architectures using atomic-stage interventions, revealing that many failures stem from poor target grounding and global spatial routing, while local manipulation skills remain largely usable. Based on these findings, we propose MFM-VLA, a selective collaboration framework in which an MFM provides target grounding and spatial guidance, controllers execute free-space motion, and the VLA retains control over fine-grained manipulation. We fine-tune the VLA with action-chunk-level dense geometric captions and perturbed-state recovery data to improve local guidance following and recovery from unfamiliar handoff states. A development-calibrated capability router selects between direct VLA execution and MFM-assisted execution to avoid unnecessary intervention. Across LIBERO-PRO, ALOHA-Sim-PRO, RoboCasa365, and real-world chemistry tasks, MFM-VLA improves success rates by 14.9, 74.0, 3.6, and 30.9 percentage points, respectively, over the corresponding base VLA. The project page is available at https://tom-zgt.github.io/MFM-VLA

AI.brief_summary: 论文用原子阶段干预分析多个 VLA 架构的空间泛化失败来源，发现瓶颈在目标定位与全局空间路由而非局部操作，进而提出 MFM-VLA：由多模态基础模型提供目标定位和空间引导，VLA 保留精细操作，并用能力路由器决定是否介入。
AI.relevance_reason: 其分阶段干预定位失败环节、以及按能力选择是否调用外部模块的路由器，可能可供核查 LVR 中视觉证据筛选、贡献分配与「何时停止/介入」决策的借鉴，但研究对象是机器人动作策略而非 latent 推理状态。
